items.s: Policy & Money in Thailand Net billing, incentives, payback and price Does Thailand give net metering to homeowners?Not true net metering. Thailand uses net billing: the solar power you use yourself replaces grid power at the full retail price, and the surplus you export is bought at a fixed lower rate. Units are not swapped one-for-one. How much do I get for power I sell back?2.20 baht per unit (kWh) under the household "Solar for the People" scheme, with up to 5 kW of export per meter. items.s: Choosing Your System Type, size and what to expect On-grid, hybrid or off-grid: which one?On-grid: lowest cost, fastest payback, no backup. Hybrid: adds a battery for night use and blackout backup. Off-grid: for sites with no utility supply; needs larger battery and usually a generator. Will my solar work during a blackout?A standard on-grid inverter switches off for safety when the grid fails. items.s: Installation Basics Design and workmanship points What about shading?One shaded panel can pull down a whole string. We design around shade, or use optimisers or microinverters on the affected panels. Why do connectors matter so much?Mismatched or badly crimped MC4 connectors are the most common cause of rooftop solar fires. We use the same brand on both sides and the correct crimp tool. Will installation make my roof leak?Not if done properly. Metal roofs use clamps or sealed screws on the ribs; tile roofs use hooks under the tile. items.s: Field Troubleshooting Guide Detailed answers on strings, cables, insulation, CT, meter and system control Panels on different angle/tilt: how should I lay the panels?Keep every panel in one series string on the same orientation and tilt, and give each roof face its own MPPT input. In a series string the current is set by the weakest panel, so one shaded or differently-facing panel drags the whole string down. items.s: Safety & Protection Surge, earthing and fire safety What surge protection (SPD) do you install?Type II SPD on both DC and AC sides. AC SPD to IEC 61643-11 in the distribution board; DC SPD to IEC 61643-31 in the combiner box or at the inverter DC input. What ratings should a Type II SPD have?Tested with an 8/20 microsecond wave. Nominal discharge current (In) 20 kA, maximum (Imax) 40 kA or more. AC continuous voltage (Uc) such as 275/320/420 V AC; DC rating (Ucpv) 600 or 1000 V DC, at or above the string's maximum open-circuit voltage. items.t: Straight answers. — Solar ESS | Solar Consulting, Design, Installation & Maintenance Across Thailand
items.s: FAQ Straight answers. Does Thailand give net metering to homeowners?Not true net metering. Thailand uses net billing: the solar power you use yourself replaces grid power at the full retail price, and the surplus you export is bought at a fixed lower rate of 2.20 baht per unit. How long is the payback for a home?Typically about 4 to 7 years for an on-grid system when most solar is used in the daytime. Batteries lengthen payback but add backup and night-time use. items.t: We install all sorts of brands: Huawei first, with five alternatives we trust — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Inverters We install all sorts of brands: Huawei first, with five alternatives we trust The right brand depends on the site: roof shading, phase balance, battery plans and budget. The inverter is the heart of a solar system. It turns the DC power from the panels into the AC power your home or business uses, decides when to charge the battery or draw from the grid, and shuts the system down safely when something is wrong. It is also the part most likely to need attention over 20 years, so we choose on service first and price second. Hybrid inverter with batteryInverter and AC/DC combiner boxInd

items.t: Back-contact panels from LONGi and AIKO — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Solar panels Back-contact panels from LONGi and AIKO The newest step in a long line of improvements. Here is how panels got to this point. Each generation of solar panel has turned a little more of the same sunlight into electricity. Amorphous and thin filmA thin layer of silicon or another material laid on glass or a flexible sheet. Cheap and light, and familiar from pocket calculators, but low in output, so a roof needed a large area for little power. MonocrystallineCells cut from a single silicon crystal. More power from the same area and a longer life, which made mono the standard for roof

items.t: AIKO or LONGi? — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Compared · October 2026 AIKO or LONGi? On technology the two are almost a tie. Both lose 0.26% of power per °C, age at the same rate and carry the same 15-year product and 30-year performance warranties. In the same size frame, the AIKO sold in Thailand gives 670 W against 650 W for the LONGi. On price there is no clear winner: in Thai shops both cost about the same per watt. LONGi is the larger company, shipping about three times as many panels. We choose between them by roof space and the supplier price on the day. Download the full comparison (PDF, English)

items.s: Battery Intellihome, LV Topsun G4, Flex Core ID and Dyness Sized to your evening load and the backup you need, not the biggest box on offer. A battery is only as good as its conversation with the inverter. items.t: CHINT MCCB, ABB and IPG — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Breakers CHINT MCCB, ABB and IPG Sized to the cable and the inverter on every circuit, DC and AC. A breaker is cheap until the day it has to work. This is the wrong place to save money. What we fit AC breakersABB, IPG DC breakersSUNTREE DC fuse holdersSUNTREE MCCB, main and changeover boardsCHINT Why we pick it Each breaker is matched to the cable it protects, so the breaker trips before the cable overheats. DC circuits get breakers rated for DC. An AC breaker on a DC string cannot be relied on to break the current. Labelled and laid out in the box so the next electrician can see what each one

items.t: SUNTREE gPV fuses on every string — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Fuses SUNTREE gPV fuses on every string Solar-rated DC fuses in touch-safe holders. The fuse is the cheapest part in the DC box, and the one that stops a string fault becoming a fire. What we fit DC fusesSUNTREE, gPV class, rated for the system DC voltage Fuse holdersSUNTREE, touch-safe Why we pick it gPV fuses are made to clear the low fault currents a solar string produces. An AC fuse is not. Fitted on both the positive and negative lines where strings run in parallel. The rating is chosen above the string current and within the panel maker's maximum series fuse rating. Holders open safely t

items.t: SUNTREE surge protection on both the DC and AC sides — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Surge protection (SPD) SUNTREE surge protection on both the DC and AC sides Fitted in the DC and AC boxes, with a proper earth. An inverter is electronics. Surge protection costs a small fraction of the inverter it saves. What we fit SPDSUNTREE, DC and AC Why we pick it Thai storm seasons bring lightning surges down both the roof cables and the grid line. Protecting one side only leaves the inverter exposed. Installed close to the equipment with a short, direct earth connection, which is what makes the device effective. Checked at every maintenance visit. Product sheet (PDF): English · ภาษาไทย

items.t: An ATS rated for the full load, chosen per project — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Automatic transfer switch (ATS) An ATS rated for the full load, chosen per project Used where a site has backup power, a generator or more than one supply. The ATS is a safety device as much as a convenience. We size it to the site, not to a price list. What we fit ATSGEYA, CSQ, SUNTREE Why we pick it Switches the load between sources by itself, so the lights come back without anyone going to the board. items.s: Wiring Neat, labelled and built to be serviced How the cables are run matters as much as which cables we buy. Most faults we are called to on other installers' systems start at a connector or a loose terminal. items.s: Grounding system One earth, measured and recorded Panel frames, rails, boxes and the inverter all bonded to a tested earth. Surge protection and leakage protection only work if the earth behind them is real. What we fit Earth rodsCopper-bonded ground rods Earth conductorGreen/yellow copper, sized to the circuit BondingEvery panel frame, rail joint and metal box Why we pick it Bonding the frames and rails means a fault cannot leave exposed metal live. items.t: The inverter maker's own meter, at the grid connection — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Smart meter The inverter maker's own meter, at the grid connection Needed for zero export, battery control and accurate self-consumption figures. The inverter can only control what it can measure. What we fit MeterThe meter specified by the inverter maker, single-phase or three-phase to match the supply LocationAt the grid connection point, after the PEA meter Why we pick it Zero export and export limits depend on it. items.t: Current transformers and monitoring sensors — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Sensors Current transformers and monitoring sensors The small parts that tell the system, and us, what is really happening. One CT clipped the wrong way round can make a good system look broken. What we fit Current sensors (CT)The inverter maker's own CTs, sized to the main breaker Monitoring sensorsIrradiance and panel-temperature sensors on larger plants, on request Why we pick it Each CT goes on the right conductor, facing the right way, on its matching phase. Split-core CTs let us fit them to an existing board without cutting the supply. Irradiance and temperature readings let us judge out

items.t: KJL steel boxes — Recommended Solar Panels, Inverters & Batteries
items.s: Enclosures KJL steel boxes For the AC and DC combiner boxes beside the inverter. The box keeps water, dust and hands away from live parts for the life of the system. What we fit EnclosureKJL, steel Why we pick it Steel stands up to heat and knocks better than plastic, and gives a solid earth point. Sized with room inside, so breakers and surge protection run cool and can be serviced. items.t: October–November 2026 · SolisCloud · CT and battery review: 10 plants – one meter missing 60% of grid import, one battery held full — Solar Technical Notes & Monthly Plant Reports
items.s: Monthly report · 12 pages · PDF · English October–November 2026 · SolisCloud · CT and battery review: 10 plants – one meter missing 60% of grid import, one battery held full A review of 10 plants Solar ESS monitors on SolisCloud, from daily data for 1 October – 8 November and 5-minute profiles for 5 and 8 November. CTs are correct at nine plants; at a Chiang Rai resort the meter's import counter records only about 40% of what the site actually buys.
